audits.title: Unmet needs in patients with epilepsy, following audit, educational intervention and the introduction of the New General Practice Contract.
audits.standard: New General Practice Contract epilepsy quality indicators (annual review, seizure frequency documentation)

cycle1.result: Baseline annual review and seizure frequency documentation (figures not stated); 22% under shared care.

audits.intervention: Letter summarising findings, comprehensive template, individual patient categorisation, neurologist-led educational session (March 2004) and New Contract (April 2004)

cycle2.result: Significant, sustained increase in annual review rate and documentation of seizure frequency; shared care fell to 16%.

audits.other_findings: 30 of 62 (48%) poorly controlled patients were not under shared care; 13 referrals and 32 practice interventions with 39 positive outcomes.
audits.citation: Minshall I, Smith D. Unmet needs in patients with epilepsy, following audit, educational intervention and the introduction of the New General Practice Contract. Prim Health Care Res Dev. 2012;13(1):85-91. doi:10.1017/s1463423611000351. PMID: 21896230.

audits.title: Towards the development of integrated epilepsy services: an audit of documented epilepsy care.
audits.setting: 53 general practices, Mid-West region of Ireland

cycle1.result: Neurologist confirmation of diagnosis documented in 132 (35%); 282 (75%) had no documented specialist review; 149 (40%) not reviewed by GP for epilepsy in previous two years.

audits.other_findings: Significant variation in documentation of epilepsy-specific information.
audits.citation: Varley J, O'Connor R, Delanty N, O'Riordan D, Kenny A, Barry N, et al.. Towards the development of integrated epilepsy services: an audit of documented epilepsy care. Ir Med J. 2011;104(7):214-217. PMID: 21957690.

audits.title: An audit of treated epilepsy in Glasgow. West of Scotland Epilepsy Research Group.
audits.standard: Documentation of epilepsy diagnosis, seizure control and history in treated epilepsy

cycle1.result: Current seizure control documented in only 39% of records; in 24% no record of who made the diagnosis; birth injury, febrile convulsions and family history not mentioned in over 80%.

audits.other_findings: 76% on monotherapy; 29% diagnosed by a neurologist; a standard record form was recommended.
audits.citation: Muir TM, Bradley A, Wood SF, Murray GD, Brodie MJ. An audit of treated epilepsy in Glasgow. West of Scotland Epilepsy Research Group. Seizure. 1996;5(1):41-46. doi:10.1016/s1059-1311(96)80061-6. PMID: 8777551.

audits.title: A general practice records audit of the process of care for people with epilepsy.
audits.standard: Recommendations on provision of care for epilepsy
audits.setting: 31 randomly selected general practices in one UK health region

cycle1.result: Recording generally good but poor for key items; EEG and CT often poorly directed, therapy not always optimal, little GP review and inadequate counselling.

audits.other_findings: Suggests specialist epilepsy nurses across the primary-secondary interface.
audits.citation: Jacoby A, Graham-Jones S, Baker G, Ratoff L, Heyes J, Dewey M, et al.. A general practice records audit of the process of care for people with epilepsy. Br J Gen Pract. 1996;46(411):595-599. PMID: 8945797.

audits.title: Managing epilepsy in general practice: the dissemination and uptake of a free audit package, and collated results from 12 practices in England and Wales.
audits.standard: Epilepsy audit protocol for general practice
audits.setting: 12 general practices in England and Wales

cycle1.result: 60% seizure free, 11% more than one seizure per month; 71% on monotherapy; 88% with ongoing seizures seen by GP in last 12 months; lifestyle information given and noted in 18%.

audits.other_findings: Of 215 practices requesting the protocol, 47 (28%) collected data and 12 (7%) submitted data matching the protocol; recording of seizure frequency was low.
audits.citation: Chappell B, Hall WW. Managing epilepsy in general practice: the dissemination and uptake of a free audit package, and collated results from 12 practices in England and Wales. Seizure. 1997;6(1):9-12. doi:10.1016/s1059-1311(97)80046-5. PMID: 9061817.

audits.title: An audit of the management of patients with epilepsy in thirty general practices.

cycle1.result: Use of drug monotherapy and anticonvulsant blood level monitoring was sub-optimal (figures not reported in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Doctors lacked detailed awareness of how epilepsy affected patients, and many patients had difficulty communicating anxieties to their GP.
audits.citation: Cooper GL, Huitson A. An audit of the management of patients with epilepsy in thirty general practices. J R Coll Gen Pract. 1986;36(286):204-208. PMID: 3746763.

audits.title: Medical audit of the care of patients with epilepsy in one group practice.

cycle1.result: Less than half on monotherapy; insufficient counselling; serum drug levels affected management in 70%; 9 of 17 patients with problems not regularly followed up.

audits.other_findings: Over half felt unacceptable to society; patients rather than doctors set consultation frequency in half.
audits.citation: Jones AL. Medical audit of the care of patients with epilepsy in one group practice. J R Coll Gen Pract. 1980;30(216):396-400. PMID: 7441631.
